title: Berar Sultanate
capsule: The Berar Sultanate (Sultanate of Berar, capital Ellichpur) was one of the five successor states formed by the breakup of the Bahmani Sultanate of the Deccan, established when the governor Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk declared independence around 1490. The sultanate controlled a compact but agriculturally productive territory in the upper Wardha valley, known for cotton cultivation, and maintained its independence through alliances with the other Deccan Sultanates against Vijayanagara. It was the first of the Deccan Sultanates to lose its independence, annexed by the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574 under Murtaza Nizam Shah I, who exploited a succession dispute to absorb Berar's territory.
